tldr: MindForge is a generative-agent framework that enables open-weight LLM-powered embodied agents to improve through social collaboration using Theory of Mind, significantly outperforming isolated Voyager baselines in Minecraft tasks.
contributions: A structured Theory of Mind representation (BigToM causal template) linking percepts, beliefs, desires, and actions
Natural language inter-agent communication integrated with Minecraft's chat system
A multi-component memory system with episodic, semantic, and procedural memory subsystems
Demonstration that open-weight LLMs can match GPT-4 performance through collaboration alone
methods: The authors extend the Voyager framework by adding (1) a BigToM causal template for structured self-modeling and partner perspective-taking, (2) natural-language communication via Minecraft's chat system using Mineflayer API, and (3) three memory subsystems (episodic, semantic, procedural) inspired by the Soar cognitive architecture. They evaluate in Minecraft using MineDojo, measuring success over 24 independent trials for isolated tasks and tracking tech-tree milestones and unique items collected. Experiments include instructive settings (mixed-expertise with GPT-4 seeding) and collaborative settings (matched-expertise weak-weak agents).
results: In instructive settings with GPT-4, MindForge agents achieve 3× more tech-tree milestones and collect 2.3× more unique items than the Voyager baseline. Open-weight LLMs (Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B, Llama 3.1-8B) without collaboration achieve only 4-27% success on basic dirt/wood collection tasks versus 100% for GPT-4; with MindForge, Mistral-7B reaches 37.5% (dirt) and 33.3% (wood). In weak-weak collaborative settings, a single round of GPT-4 seeding followed by seven turns of peer dialogue raises population-level success from 62% to 79%, consistent with the Condorcet Jury Theorem.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to Minecraft environments
Instructive settings require GPT-4 for initial seeding/expert support
Open-weight LLMs without collaboration struggle with even rudimentary tasks (4-27% success on basic tasks)
The approach relies on test-time compute scaling through communication rather than reducing training/fine-tuning needs entirely
